lessons.title: 223. Ch 16 · Grammar C: simultaneous actions or conditions with -(으)면서
lessons.subtitle: 샤워하면서 노래해요 · 책을 읽으면서 커피 마셔요 · 의사이면서 교수 · 싸면서 예뻐요

explanations.title: Expressing simultaneous actions or conditions
explanations.body:
In English, we often express concurrent actions or conditions by using while or at the same time, as in “He is having breakfast while watching TV” or “He is lazy but, at the same time, smart.” In Korean, we express simultaneous actions or conditions by using the conjunctive ending -(으)면서: 저는 샤워하면서 노래해요 (I sing while taking a shower); 장 선생님은 의사이면서 교수이십니다 (Mr. Chang is a doctor and (at the same time) a professor).

Keep in mind that -(으)면서 is used only when multiple actions or conditions are done by or exist for the same subject.

rows: When a verb stem ends in a vowel
When a verb stem ends in a consonant
책을 읽다 + 커피 마시다 → 책을 읽으면서 커피 마시다

explanations.title: Forms
explanations.body: The forms below are mine, made by the book’s rule (a stem ending in ㄹ keeps it before 면서: 놀다 → 놀면서; the ㄷ irregular verbs 듣다 and 걷다 change ㄷ to ㄹ: 들으면서, 걸으면서). After a noun the copula 이다 is used: 의사이면서.

explanations.title: Follow-up 1: a chain of simultaneous actions
explanations.body: In the book the students sit in a circle: the first starts with a simple phrase like 샤워합니다; the next changes it to 샤워하면서 and adds another phrase, and so on. The book’s model, with the students A–D named 철수, 영희, 민수 and 지영 here (the English is mine):

examples.translation: cheolsu: syawohamnida. — I take a shower.
yeonghui: syawohamyeonseo eumageul deutseumnida. — I listen to music while taking a shower.
minsu: eumageul deureumyeonseo keopireul masimnida. — I drink coffee while listening to music.
jiyeong: keopireul masimyeonseo chinguwa iyagihamnida. — I talk with a friend while drinking coffee.

explanations.title: Follow-up 2: two lists
explanations.body: In the book one partner reads a phrase from List A, the other changes it into -(으)면서 and adds a phrase from List B (the sentence must make sense). List A: 군인이다, 학생이다, 선생님이다, 공무원이다, 주부이다; List B: 아내이다, 간호사이다, 아들이다, 아버지이다, 의사이다. The book’s model: 군인이다 → 이 병장은 군인이면서 학생입니다. (Sergeant Lee is a soldier and a student.) The five sentences below are mine.

Mr. Park is a student and a nurse.
Mr. Lee is a teacher and a father.

Ms. Han is a housewife and a doctor.

lessons.title: 224. Ch 16 · Grammar D: realization and discovery with -(는)군요 and -네요
lessons.subtitle: 재미있군요 · 재미있네요 · 멋있네요 · 예쁘군요 · 의사이시군요 · 마시는군요

explanations.title: Verb endings that express realization or discovery
explanations.body: In English, when we come to a realization or discover a certain fact, we often say something like, “Wow, she is beautiful!” or “Wow, this is strange!” Koreans express this by using -(는)군요 or -네요. Compare the following sentences:

examples.translation: hangungmari jaemiisseoyo. — Korean is fun. (a simple statement: the speaker already knows)
hangungmari jaemiitgunyo! — (Wow) Korean is fun! (with -군요)
hangungmari jaemiinneyo! — (Wow) Korean is fun! (with -네요)

explanations.title: What the endings imply
explanations.body: The first sentence is a simple statement that implies the speaker already knows that Korean is fun. However, the last two sentences, which end in -(는)군요 and -네요, tell us that the speaker just realized or discovered that Korean is fun. This implies that the speaker did not know that Korean was fun until the moment of the utterance.

rows: With stative verbs and 이다/아니다 or 있다/없다
멋있다 → 멋있군요 / 멋있네요!; 예쁘다 → 예쁘군요 / 예쁘네요!; 학생이다 → 학생이군요 / 학생이네요!
With an action verb in the present tense
피아노를 잘 치다 → 피아노를 잘 치는군요 / 치네요!; 커피를 마시다 → 커피를 마시는군요 / 마시네요!

explanations.title: How to use this list
explanations.body:
The book’s Core Vocabulary lists the core words of the chapter with an example sentence for each (the sentences and the English meanings are the book’s; the book gives no English for the sentences). The Hanja of the Sino-Korean words are in parentheses before the meaning. Optional parts, such as (~하다/되다), are kept in the meanings.

The example sentences with digits are respelled in Hangul (24시간 → 이십사 시간, 10,000원 → 만 원, 5,000원 → 오천 원, 5월 5일 → 오월 오일, 75만원 → 칠십오만 원, 5천 → 오천); the book’s 연기 appears twice (延期, postponement, and 煙氣, smoke) and is shown once for each meaning. The book’s related words (the synonyms, antonyms and related words in the last column) are not repeated. The book’s Additional Vocabulary table is empty: it is for your own words.

explanations.title: Self-evaluation
explanations.body:
Recall the objectives of the chapter and ask yourself whether you have achieved them (the book asks you to tick Yes or No). If you tick “No” for any item, the book suggests: review that section on your own; find a study partner and review it as a pair or group; and tell your academic advisor or team leader which areas you need more help with, so that they can provide activities tailored to your learning style and needs.

Now I am able to: make a domestic flight reservation; ask for and give information about a travel package; ask for and give information about renting a car; report simple car problems; identify simple automotive parts; talk about well-known tourist attractions in Korea.

Now I have a clear understanding of: the new words and phrases in the Core Vocabulary; 아무나 or 아무 ~(이)나 in the affirmative (any ~); 아무나 or 아무 ~(이)나 in the negative (not just any ~); -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 (know how to); -(으)ㄹ 줄 모르다 (not know how to); the exclamatory verb endings -군요 and -네요; the conjunctive ending -(으)면서, used to express simultaneous actions or conditions; the Sino-Korean syllables 불/부 (不), 적 (的), and 형 (型).
